quotes.text: Customers have up to 180 calendar days to file a dispute from the date of capture.
Fraudulent transactions are one example of this immediate escalation, but there are also other scenarios.

Refunding during the inquiry dispute period avoids a dispute fee and prevents the inquiry from being escalated to a chargeback dispute. Refunds can no longer be performed after the inquiry escalates to a chargeback dispute.
Businesses have 12 calendar days from chargeback escalation to provide evidence, except for fraud disputes, which have a 5 day timeframe.
You can submit evidence on the dispute, but you can’t simulate the final dispute outcome in a sandbox.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/disputes, a Klarna customer files an order complaint or return request in the Klarna app within 180 calendar days of capture, subject to listed exceptions. Most cases enter a 21-day inquiry: merchant contact or refund of the disputed amount can resolve it, but evidence is accepted only after chargeback escalation, when funds and the fee are withheld and 12-day evidence applies, or five days for fraud. API statuses distinguish inquiry from chargeback and won/lost states; sandbox triggers cannot simulate final outcomes. These boundaries are present in old raw lines 10-89 and new raw lines 11-111, 245-247, 527-569. source-stripe-klarna-disputes.md summarizes most mechanics but needs newer provenance and narrower wording about fraud and seven test scenarios.
